hints.title: Large Integer Overflow Obstacle
hints.text: Converting lists to standard integers fails on 100-digit values due to precision limits. How can you accumulate digits along with incoming carry values directly as you step forward?

hints.title: Digit-by-Digit Addition Invariant
hints.text: Maintain a running carry value while advancing whichever list node is non-null, creating a new result digit node at each step.

hints.title: Sequential Carry Step Procedure
hints.text: Create a dummy head node. Loop while list 1 or list 2 is not null or carry is non-zero. Sum the existing carry plus available node values, update carry to sum integer-divided by 10, and append a new node with value sum modulo 10. Advance each pointer when valid.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def addTwoNumbers(self, l1: Optional[ListNode], l2: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        dummy = ListNode(0)
        curr = dummy
        carry = 0
        while l1 or l2 or carry:
            val1 = l1.val if l1 else 0
            val2 = l2.val if l2 else 0
            total = val1 + val2 + carry
            carry = total // 10
            curr.next = ListNode(total % 10)
            curr = curr.next
            if l1: l1 = l1.next
            if l2: l2 = l2.next
        return dummy.next
```

complexity.notes: Digit-by-digit simulation creates max(N, M) + 1 nodes at most.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Reconstructing full numeric integers overflows 64-bit integer ranges when linked lists exceed 19 digits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Streaming digit addition directly into a new linked list ensures strict O(max(N, M)) runtime and memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Proper handling of asymmetric input lengths, dummy sentinel head node usage, and leftover final carry.
